messages:
emma: Quick sync - we need an autoscale governance playbook for Dedicated. Top asks: explainability for every autoscale decision, billing correlation, and a customer-safe policy editor.
rick: +1. Customers want to know why we prewarmed, what the alternatives were, and the cost impact. Also good for oncall to debug.
finance-bot: billing requirement: every prewarm/reservation or aggressive autoscale must have a reservation_id and be linked to invoice lines. Decision traces should include cost_estimate_usd.
ops-oncall: ops needs an immutable decision log (DECISION_TRACE) per action with latency and health signals. Must include fallback chosen and reason. Also require kill-switch hooks and an automatic rollback if prewarm attempts fail repeatedly.
legal: SA and SLA teams: any customer-facing policy editor that lets them choose deterministic prewarm will need explicit contract language and refund rules. We need a clear default: best-effort unless contract says otherwise.
emma: proposal sketch: a policy bundle + explainability payload. Policy bundles are versioned and tenant-scoped. Explainability payload is a short human-readable "why" plus structured fields. Example below.

```
policy_bundle:
  id: pb-2026-0001
  name: customer_slo_first_v1
  scope: tenant
  rules:
    - rule_id: r1_ramp_prewarm
      match: predicted_p95_latency_ms > 200
      action: prewarm(count=2, type=best_effort)
      cost_estimate_usd: 1.25
      fallback: increase_batch
```

explainability_payload (for every decision):
- decision_id: dt-0001
- policy_bundle_id: pb-2026-0001
- rule_id: r1_ramp_prewarm
- why: "predicted_p95 > 200ms based on last 10m qps trend; prewarm chosen to protect tail latency"
- inputs: [predicted_p95=220, burst_credit_pct=12]
- cost_estimate_usd: 1.25
- action_taken: prewarm(count=2,type=best_effort)
- fallback_action: increase_batch_size
- correlation_ids: [reservation_id, invoice_line_id]
```

rick: I like the human "why" field. For Console UX we can surface a short sentence plus a link to the full trace. Also expose decision_id in request headers so customers can reference it in support tickets.
finance-bot: please ensure invoice_line_id appears in DECISION_TRACE before charging. Also tag prewarm nodes with reservation_id so billing can reconcile node-hours.
ops-oncall: runtime guardrails: - prewarm_fail_counter window: if >3 failures in 30m -> auto-disable prewarm for tenant for 1h and route to conservative mode. - canary rollout: apply policy to 1% traffic for 10m then ramp. - store DECISION_TRACE to immutable event store for 90d.
legal: default policy must be best-effort. deterministic prewarm only via contract opt-in. Refund formula needs to be in SLA draft; product should draft sample wording.
emma: prioritization & roadmap: 1) spike (1w) to add DECISION_TRACE skeleton in runtime+billing correlation; 2) 2-week sprint to wire Console link + decision_id in headers; 3) canary with 2 lighthouse tenants; 4) contract add-on for deterministic prewarm after GA.
rick: staffing ask: 2 runtime engs, 1 billing eng, 1 frontend, 1 ops for canary.
ops-oncall: observability: dashboard with recent DECISION_TRACE entries, prewarm_success_rate, and a page if decision traces per-minute > baseline * 5.
emma: launch criteria draft: - DECISION_TRACE emitted for every autoscale action - cost_estimate and invoice_line_id present - Console surfaces explainability + link to trace - decision_id in response headers - rollback & kill-switch tested in canary - legal signoff for deterministic option.
product-bot: Created tickets: #PL-4999 (spike: decision trace), #ENG-4990 (billing correlation), #FE-1010 (Console trace link), #OPS-1600 (canary runbook).
rick: action items: emma owns spike; ops-oncall owns runbook; finance-bot prep sample invoice lines; legal draft SLA snippet.
emma: thanks. I'll also draft a short customer-facing FAQ explaining what "best-effort" vs "deterministic" means and how costs are calculated.
